paths.title: Rendering and Performance
paths.description: Understand how browsers build pixels, then reduce work that delays loading and interaction.
concept: Browsers transform HTML and CSS into pixels through parsing, style calculation, layout, paint, and compositing.
JavaScript, fonts, images, and style changes can interrupt or repeat parts of this pipeline. Performance work starts by identifying which stage is expensive.
workflow: Diagnose a slow interaction
Measure the user-visible delay before changing code.
Use browser tooling to connect a slow click or scroll to scripting, layout, painting, network, or memory work.
Reproduce the delay with a consistent action.
Record a performance trace.
Locate the longest main-thread tasks.
Check whether layout or paint repeats unnecessarily.
Inspect network requests and image sizes.
Change one cause and measure again.
question: Avoid unnecessary layout work
Which change is most likely to trigger layout for many elements?
Changing text color
Reading and writing element dimensions repeatedly inside a loop
Updating an aria-label
Adding a console message
Interleaving layout reads and writes can force repeated synchronous layout calculations.
checklist: Frontend performance baseline
Confirm that the page loads and responds without avoidable work.
Performance should be evaluated on realistic mobile hardware and networks.
Critical content appears without waiting for optional scripts.
Images use appropriate dimensions and modern formats.
Long tasks are split or deferred.
Layout shifts are prevented with reserved space.
Repeated DOM work is batched.
The result is measured after each optimization.

paths.title: Forms and Client Data
paths.description: Build accessible forms, validate input, and represent loading, success, and failure states clearly.
concept: A reliable form combines native controls, labels, constraints, feedback, and a predictable submission lifecycle.
Client-side validation improves usability, but the server remains authoritative. The interface must preserve entered values and explain corrections.
workflow: Implement a resilient submission flow
Treat submission as a state machine instead of a single click handler.
Explicit states prevent duplicate requests and unclear feedback.
Associate every control with a visible label.
Validate required formats before submission.
Disable only the duplicate action.
Show a submitting state.
Handle field and general errors separately.
Restore interaction after failure.
Confirm success clearly.
question: Place validation responsibility correctly
Where must business-critical input validation be enforced?
Only in HTML attributes
Only in browser JavaScript
On the server, with optional matching client checks
Only after data is stored
Browser checks can be bypassed. The server must enforce the actual contract.
checklist: Accessible form review
Verify the form with keyboard, semantics, and failure states.
A form is complete only when users can understand errors and recover.
Every input has an associated label.
Required fields are communicated in text and semantics.
Errors identify the field and correction.
Focus moves only when it helps recovery.
Submitting twice cannot create duplicate work.
Mobile input modes are appropriate.
Success is announced clearly.

paths.title: Testing and Delivery
paths.description: Test behavior at the right level and release frontend changes without breaking users.
concept: Frontend tests are most durable when they verify what users can see and do rather than private implementation details.
Use unit tests for isolated logic, integration tests for component behavior, and browser tests for critical journeys.
workflow: Build a release confidence ladder
Run fast checks first and broader checks before deployment.
A layered pipeline catches simple defects early while still protecting real user journeys.
Run formatting and syntax checks.
Run unit tests for pure logic.
Run integration tests for interactive states.
Test keyboard and accessibility behavior.
Exercise critical browser journeys.
Build the production bundle.
Verify the deployed preview on narrow and wide screens.
question: Choose the correct test level
Which test best verifies that a user can submit a form and see a saved record after a real API response?
A unit test for a string formatter
A CSS snapshot only
A browser-level end-to-end test
A linter rule
The behavior crosses UI, network, and persistence boundaries, so a browser-level journey should own it.
checklist: Safe frontend release
Confirm that the deployed artifact behaves like the reviewed preview.
Deployment can differ from local development because of caching, environment values, and asset paths.
The production build completes cleanly.
No browser-exposed secret is bundled.
Asset and route URLs work from the deployed base path.
The service worker updates compatible files.
Critical journeys pass against the preview.
Errors are observable after release.
A rollback path is known.
